title: Persistence, resetting, and first-passage times of an active Ornstein--Uhlenbeck particle
authors: Demosthenes K. Georgiou, Paul C. Bressloff, Thibault Bertrand
abstract: We study the first-passage time statistics of an active Ornstein--Uhlenbeck particle on a finite one-dimensional interval with an absorbing boundary at one end and a reflecting boundary at the other, subject to stochastic resetting. In the weak-activity regime, we develop a perturbative solution of the Fokker--Planck equation and use a renewal framework to obtain analytical expressions for the first-passage-time distribution and its low-order moments. In the absence of resetting, activity can either increase or decrease the mean first-passage time, depending on the relation between the persistence time and the diffusive time to absorption. When resetting is introduced, we determine both the onset of beneficial resetting and the finite range of resetting rates for which resetting lowers the mean first-passage time of the active system. We further show that the resetting transition depends on the velocity resetting protocol. Finally, by comparing the active particle with resetting to the passive Brownian particle without resetting, we construct a phase diagram that identifies the regions of parameter space in which activity and resetting together reduce the mean first-passage time.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how the mean first-passage time of an active particle is affected by intrinsic activity and external stochastic resetting. Using perturbative methods on the Fokker-Planck equation, the authors map out parameter regimes where the combination of activity and resetting can synergistically accelerate the process towards an absorbing boundary.
main_problem: The study investigates the statistics of first-passage times (FPT) for an active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particle confined to a 1D interval with specific boundary conditions, incorporating stochastic resetting.
main_result: The paper determines the conditions under which activity and resetting together reduce the mean first-passage time, identifying a phase diagram controlling this reduction.
method: The analysis employs perturbative solutions to the Fokker-Planck equation in the weak-activity regime, utilizing a renewal framework for the resetting dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is an active Ornstein-Uhlenbeck particle (AOUP) confined to $[0, L]$, featuring an absorbing boundary at one end and a reflecting boundary at the other. Stochastic resetting is added to the dynamics.
key_observables: Mean First-Passage Time (MFPT), survival probability, and the FPT density.
important_parameters: Diffusivity ($D$), persistence time ($	au_p$), activity strength ($p$), and the resetting rate ($r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the weak-activity regime ($	ext{Pe} \ll 1$), and Poissonian resetting is assumed.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the AOUP trajectory, boundaries, and the effect of resetting. Figure C1 shows the relative error decreasing as persistence time increases.
paper_structure: The paper develops the dynamics via the Fokker-Planck equation, solves it perturbatively in the weak-activity limit, applies renewal theory for resetting, and analyzes the resulting MFPT dependence on activity and resetting rates.
why_interesting: While focused on classical active matter, the mathematical techniques involving non-equilibrium dynamics, boundary value problems, and the interplay between external driving (activity) and external intervention (resetting) are highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum control theory.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic trajectory of an active Ornstein–Uhlenbeck particle on the interval [0, L], with an absorbing boundary at x = 0 and a reflecting boundary at x = L. Resetting returns the particle to x0, and the propulsion velocity is reset according to the chosen protocol.

Figure 2. MFPT without resetting as a function of x0/L for (a) τ = 0.25 and (b) τp = 1 for the values of Pe indicated in the figure. Solid lines show the perturbative approximation to O(Pe2) and symbols show simulation results.
Figure 4. MFPT without resetting for fixed initial velocities, for (a) v0 = +1 and (b) v0 = −1 for τp = 0.25 and the values of Pe indicated in the figure. The results are obtained from simulations.

Figure 5. MFPT Tr as a function of the resetting rate r for varying values of x0/L, at fixed τp = 1, and Pe = 1. The solid curves show the perturbative prediction to O(Pe2), and the symbols are the simulation results. Depending on the initial position, the dependence on r is either monotonic or non-monotonic.

Figure 6. FPT distributions for (a) x0/L = 0.25 and (b) x0/L = 0.75 at fixed Pe = 1 and τp = 1. Solid lines and symbols denote the theory and simulations results respectively. Resetting suppresses the long-time tail when it is beneficial, but delays absorption when it interrupts trajectories that would otherwise reach the target.
